text.p: These are significant stories in the Nigerian press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Distressed banks owe central bank 15 billion naira, says the apex bank's deputy governor Victor Odozi.

- Nigerians resident in the United States back "Vision 2010" programme and have suggested 20 areas in which the committee charged with drawing up the plan to make Nigeria a great nation should focus on.
- Weekly demand for forex falls to $31.98 million this week from $44 million last week.

- Lagos state military administrator Colonel Mohammed Marwa blames gruelling fuel crisis on state oil company Nigerian National Petroleum Corporation as succour appears far-fetched for the harried citizen.
- Oil minister Dan Etete denies claims by his finance ministry counterpart that funds voted for repair of oil refineries were misused.
- Self-proclaimed prophetess Deborah Olaosebikan sentenced to 46 years in jail for burning the hands of two sisters in a bid to excise what she called withcraft from them.
- Some 32,000 tonnes of cement is due to arrive this weekend at Lagos port on board a vessel, MV Guld Wind.

- Justice minister Michael Agbamuche, who visited Kaduna prison in the north on Thursday, avoided talking with journalist Chris Anyanwu, one of many people jailed over an alleged 1995 plot to topple the government.
- Guinea and Gambia rebuff emmisaries of soldiers who seized power in Sierra Leone last month and whom Nigeria wants to remove in order to restore the ousted elected president.
